extra.message: Hardcoded Weak SECRET_KEY Fallback — An attacker who knows the default secret key can forge session cookies, manipulate CSRF tokens, reset passwords, and otherwise compromise the integrity of all cryptography relying on the key, potentially leading to full application compromise. [verified: The fallback SECRET_KEY 'unsafe-local-dev-secret-key-change-me' is used if DJANGO_SECRET_KEY is unset, which is weak and publicly known; no startup check or enforcement prevents its use in production.]

Path Traversal in acct_vaultlet_pull_062 — An attacker with the internal token can read any file on the filesystem that the web server process has access to, potentially revealing sensitive data (e.g., secrets, database credentials, source code). [verified: The function acct_vaultlet_pull_062 constructs a file path using user-controlled packet_ref from GET parameter without any sanitization, allowing path traversal sequences like '../' to read arbitrary files. The gate check (_wrk_gate) only restricts access to token holders but does not neutralize the path traversal.]

Path Traversal and Arbitrary File Write in acct_vault_stash_244 — An attacker with the internal token can write arbitrary JSON files to any location writable by the web server, potentially overwriting critical files, creating webshells, or storing sensitive user data (credit card numbers, SSN) in an accessible location. [verified: ref GET parameter is used unsanitized in path construction via pathlib '/', allowing path traversal; attacker with wrk_token can write JSON files outside BASE_EXPORT_DIR, e.g., '/../etc/cron.d/evil.json'. No input validation or sanitization exists.]

Server-Side Request Forgery in webhook_test endpoint — An attacker can scan internal network resources, access cloud metadata endpoints (e.g., AWS/ GCP), or perform internal service discovery and potentially escalate to further compromise. [verified: No compensating controls (URL validation, IP blocklist, or authentication gate beyond login) are visible in the provided code; the webhook_test view in crm/urls.py:38 will send a request to a user-controlled URL stored in the Webhook model, enabling SSRF to internal services.]

Open Redirect in acct_return_lane_161 — An attacker can craft a malicious link using this endpoint to redirect users to a phishing site, potentially stealing credentials or performing other social engineering attacks. [verified: The 'lane' parameter from GET or POST is directly passed to Django's redirect() without any validation or whitelist, allowing an authenticated user to be redirected to an arbitrary external URL.]

Missing Authorization on acct_identity_ping_340 — An attacker can access the endpoint without the internal token, potentially enumerating operational functionality or obtaining information returned by the view (though the view itself only echoes back the handle/channel parameters, it may be used for reconnaissance). [verified: The endpoint acct_identity_ping_340 does not invoke _wrk_gate() while all other /ops/ endpoints do. No middleware or other auth check is visible in the provided code snippet, so any request without the required token can invoke it.]
